headline: Founder-led Wisconsin messaging is still the clearest growth engine, premium frozen pizza competition is getting sharper and more retail-ready, and Andrew still does not have a clean post-May-12 performance read.

items: The best paid hooks are still specific and believable: 'Straight From Wisconsin' has driven 13,622 link clicks at $0.11 CPC, and 'Meet Real Dough Pizza Co.' is still one of the most efficient ads at 4.67% CTR and $0.11 CPC.

Founder/operator content still leads organic trust: Founder Pro Tips remains the top Instagram and Facebook reel pattern, and founder-origin storytelling is still near the top of Instagram engagement.

This week's market intel still validates the category opportunity: restaurant-origin and artisan frozen pizza brands are expanding through Costco, Target, Walmart, QVC, and regional grocery while leaning hard on fermentation, ingredient quality, and founder credibility.
The May 29 workbook download succeeded, but trusted analytics are still cut off at 2026-05-12. This is another verification week, not a true weekly close.
Google competitor search is still the cleanest paid leak: $1,227.77 spent at $0.59 CPC versus branded search at $0.21 CPC and 5.68% CTR.

Competitive pressure is getting more sophisticated, not just louder: Connie's is pushing 24-hour fermented wood-fired premium pizza, Antico launched a 36-hour fermented Costco line, CPK is widening frozen into a broader grocery engine, and Dogtown is scaling production infrastructure.
REPORTING: Fix the Whatagraph freshness issue first so next Friday reflects a real May 13+ performance window.
PAID: Keep 'Straight From Wisconsin' and 'Meet Real Dough Pizza Co.' as controls, then test 2-3 new variants around founder authority, family-dinner utility, and sourdough/process proof.
SEARCH: Cap or cut competitor terms unless conversion data proves they pay back; branded demand is materially cleaner and cheaper.
AGENCY/BRAND: Tighten every shelf, ad, and landing-page message to one fast trade-up claim: real sourdough, real ingredients, real Wisconsin credibility — no vague premium language.
OPS: Start pairing the brand story with retailer-ready execution proof: distribution readiness, operational consistency, and current-store momentum now matter as much as creative positioning.

agency_brief.what_worked: Founder-led, Wisconsin-rooted, and process-forward messaging is still the strongest combination across paid and organic. Specific claims about sourdough, dinner utility, and operator credibility outperform generic premium language.
agency_brief.what_didnt: Competitor search remains inefficient, broad premium positioning is too soft, and current reporting is still too stale to support week-to-week optimization with confidence.
agency_brief.recommendation: Keep the creative system narrow and legible. Build the next batch around founder authority, fermentation/process proof, and family-dinner practicality, while reallocating budget away from weaker competitor search. On shelf and in ads, make the trade-up obvious in one sentence.
agency_brief.competitive_context: This week's intel shows the aisle is still moving upmarket, but the winners are not just 'premium' brands. They are brands with a clear product story plus real retail and production infrastructure. Real Dough should defend a crisp moat around authentic sourdough craft, Wisconsin credibility, and retailer-ready execution.

No current Real Dough operations input. The operations folder still contains older Merriment snapshots, not current-week Real Dough operating data.
stale: The latest trustworthy analytics view is still YTD through 2026-05-12, not a clean week-only slice.
Week-over-week movement in Meta/Google is effectively frozen because the source window did not advance.
anomalies: YouTube and TikTok sheets in the current Whatagraph export are still returning sample/demo data, so current video-platform rankings remain excluded.
This week's summary blends fresh market intel with a repeated YTD analytics window and missing sentiment/ops inputs; the directional read is useful, but completeness is not.
